newsitem.title: GEORGIA: British Airways begins Georgia service.
newsitem.headline: British Airways begins Georgia service.

text.p: British Airways plc began service to former Soviet Georgia on Tuesday, the first major international carrier to fly scheduled direct routes into the Transcaucasus country.

Geoff Rhodes, British Airways general manager for Russia and the CIS countries, said the company would fly on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from London Heathrow to the Georgian capital Tbilisi. The evening departure from London means return flights from Tbilisi on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays.
"We are optimistic about the service. We hope to be able to increase the number of flights to a daily basis in the course of the year," he told a news conference after the first plane landed.
Rhodes said British Airways expected business from customers engaged in oil pipeline projects currently underway in Georgia.

British Airways is using 150-seat Airbus 320 passenger craft to operate the service. Rhodes said the company's partner, British Mediterranean, was operating the planes and supplying flight crews while British Airways would handle marketing.
He said the cheapest round-trip fare would cost approximately $775. The flight takes just under five hours.
